newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: HBG says U.K building market still tough.
newsitem.headline: HBG says U.K building market still tough.

text.p: Construction firm Hollandsche Beton Groep NV said on Tuesday that the outlook for the British construction market remained difficult despite an expected upturn in building volumes.
"Volumes may well improve but margins are not expected to follow suit immediately," HBG chairman Nic de Ronde Bresser told a results news conference.
"We are a little more sceptical about the British market than others," he added.
He said HBG expected real improvements would take around two years to materialise, although faster than in Germany.
While British private sector investment in industrial buildings and offices was seen rising, public sector building volumes were seen falling.
Pressure on volumes and margins in public sector infrastructure was set to continue, HBG predicted.
De Ronde Bresser said Edmund Nuttall, HBG's UK civil and maritime engineering unit, had continued to perform well under difficult conditions.
Nuttall, a major profit generator among HBG's British operations, posted 1996 net profit of 4.1 million pounds sterling, up from a year-earlier 3.6 million.
Kyle Stewart (industry, commercial and public building) posted net profit up 0.2 million pounds sterling at 0.5 milllion on turnover down two million stg at 154 million.
GA Ltd maintained its market position in Scotland and bolstered its position in northern England.
It posted net profits of 0.3 million pounds sterling, compared with a year-earlier 0.2 million.
Together with new acquisition Higgs&Hill, GA and Kyle Stewart will be merged into a single company, HBG Construction.
De Ronde Bresser said HBG would concentrate on integrating their activities in 1997, a process which was expected to be rounded off by the end of the year.
